To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

residual stress caused by shrinkage and thermal shrinkage of a resin containing 4-methacryloyloxyethyl trimellitate anhydride occurred in the metal-resin adhesively bonded structure and the residual stress was tensile in the resin near the adhesion interface.

the residual stress in the metal-resin adhesive structure caused by polymerization of the heat-curing resin is tensile stress in the resin and the stress is higher in the specimen with the surface treatment than in that without the surface treatment.
the residual stress in the heat-cured adhesive layer was higher than in the non-adhesive layer, and that ring-like cracks in resin occurred around the metal retention holes in the adhesive layer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the analysis of stress in a resin of a metal-resin adhesive structure.
the measurement of residual stress in resin by a scanning acoustic microscopy, and the results of the measurement were discussed.
the analysis of residual stress in a resin by scanning acoustic microscopy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the residual stress caused by the shrinkage of the resin and the heat shrinkage of the metal-resin structure is the main cause of the cracks in the resin.
the residual stresses were caused by the shrinkage of the resin, and that these residual stresses affected the strength of metal-resin adhesive joints.
the residual stress in a metal-resin adhesive joint is a result of the shrinkage of the resin and is affected by the surface treatment for adhesiveness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stress in a metal-resin adhesive structure is influenced by the surface treatment for adhesiveness, the shape of the retention holes, and the thickness of the resin layer.
the tensile stress on the resin was generated at the adhesion interface and that the stress was concentrated at the retention holes.
the residual stress in the adhesive resin is the main factor in the formation of cracks in the adhesive resin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scanning acoustic microscope is a useful tool to evaluate the residual stress in a metal-resin adhesively bonded structure.
the residual stress of the metal-resin structure is affected by the polymerization shrinkage of the adhesive and the thermal expansion coefficient of the metal.
the residual stresses in the resin of a metal-resin adhesively bonded structure can be measured by scanning acoustic microscopy.
